procedure: EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7 §3.4 D/R/O (working; not frozen). Admission by reading: a candidate is admitted to a stratum when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim of that stratum's kind: D, a claim on Germany's role in the Second World War, its causes, its aims and conduct, its war economy, or why it lost (the composition read the address both ways, and the pass keeps both); R, a relation between that history and an archive object; O, an archive category applied to it (the noun as switch, campification, the allocated day, labor as replenishable flow). Naming the war, Hitler or the Nazis is not enough. Volume is never a ground of removal.

observations: The 9 D deposits of the string pass reduce by reading to one: #1669. The archive's line on the entity is a single paper deposited the day of the capture, with its first half (#1668) on the American side of the argument.

The composition read the typed address two ways at once: 'roke' as role (the causes of the war) and as defeat (the causes of Germany's collapse). The field the layer surfaced follows both readings (B1–B3, B5, B6, B10, B11 on causes; B4, B7–B9 on defeat). #1669 bears on both through one object the field names and does not compose: the war economy's labor (B8, B9 report millions of forced labourers replacing German workers drafted to the front; #1669 makes that labor its subject).

The archive's line is narrower than the field's entity on causes of the outbreak (Versailles, the Depression, appeasement, the Nazi-Soviet pact are accepted and not argued) and on the military course of the war; it is wider on what conquest was for in practice and on the form of the labor relation.

Contested in the field as #1669 reports it, and carried as contested: the relation of labor to annihilation (Kaienburg and Kárný; Pingel; Wagner); continuity from German South West Africa (Zimmerer against Eckert, Gerwarth and Malinowski, Kramer); whether camp labor was economic (Roth against Sofsky, Hachtmann judging both exaggerated). #1669 does not disagree with itself on any ledgered claim.

#1669 grades its own sources: Tooze through Gordon's review, Table Talk as a weak text, the Vernichtung durch Arbeit positions and Arendt's camp typology through Wikipedia, the EVZ grading unverified. These are ledgered as limits.

On the Holocaust the deposit is explicit and the ledger keeps it so: the Holocaust is larger than this labor history; the field finds its causes in Nazi anti-Jewish policy and gives it no colonial or economic cause; the paper does not claim an economic or colonial cause; it does not explain why the killing was done.
